messages:
alex (PM): Quick sync — we need to choose Q4 scope for the Optimize toolkit. Main asks: batching/autopilot, caching recommendations, or prompt-set driven regression detection? Customers (FinServ + Retail) pushed all three. Thoughts?

maria (eng): I vote batching first. Biggest direct cost wins and relatively bounded runtime changes.

jonathan (research): Agree batching gives immediate ROI. But regression detection depends on good prompt sets — without those, alerts are noisy.

eva (design): If we push batching autopilot, we should still ship a tiny console panel that explains why a recommendation was made. Customers ask for transparency.

sara (growth): Customers care about dollars. Retail pilot said a 10% token-cost drop would justify adoption. :money_with_wings:

kevin (cs): FinServ flagged caching concerns (PII+retention). They'll want opt-in and clear audit logs before any automatic caching.

alex (PM): Proposal: do an MVP split. Phase A (MVP): batching autopilot + inline console recommendations (explainability). Phase B: prompt-set eval infra + regression alerts with diffing and historical prompt sets. Phase C: caching policy engine + per-customer consent + KMS audit.

maria (eng): Rough dev estimates: batching autopilot ~3 sprints (runtime + integration hooks), eval infra ~4 sprints (evaluation harness + alerting), caching policies ~2 sprints + security review. Can parallelize pieces.

jonathan (research): For evals/regressions acceptance criteria propose: 1) baseline prompt-set for each pilot, 2) automated diffing that flags >5% quality drop on key metrics, 3) ability to run targeted A/B on model variants.

alex (PM): Launch criteria (for MVP batching): 1) automated batching reduced per-token cost by >=8% on pilot workloads, 2) console explanation + SDK sample, 3) 2 pilot customers signed up, 4) rollback path and regression smoke tests.

kevin (cs): Add: explicit customer consent flow for caching and a short policy doc for pilots. Also need a support runbook for when batching causes latency spikes.

eva (design): I'll mock the recommendations panel and a minimal consent modal. Aim to hand off designs next week.

alex (PM): Decision: prioritize batching/autopilot + recommendations UX as Q4 top-1, keep prompt-set evals as top-2 to follow quickly. Caching policies are high-priority but gated by security review. Can eng split into runtime and eval infra tracks?

maria (eng): Yes. We'll spin two teams: runtime (batching + autopilot) and eval infra (prompt registry + diffing). Need infra capacity estimate — I'll put numbers in the spec.

alex (PM): I'll draft the spec and acceptance criteria and open a PR today. Will also @optimize-bot to create the epic and link tasks. :thumbsup:

optimize-bot: Epic created: OPT-3472 Optimize toolkit Q4 — batching autopilot MVP. Link: https://redwood.dev/epics/OPT-3472

alex (PM): Thanks. Sara, can you confirm potential pilot customers and the two-week pilot window?

sara (growth): Retailex and FinServ contact both said yes to pilot talks. I'll schedule kickoff meetings and capture success metrics.

alex (PM): Great — if no objections by EOD I'll lock this scope and start exec comms.

kevin (cs): No objections from CS side, will prep consent language and support playbook.

maria (eng): One ask: please prioritize a small telemetry schema for batching decisions so we can A/B and measure cost/latency tradeoffs.

alex (PM): Noted. I'll add telemetry req to the spec. Closing thread after PR posted.
